newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU agrees longer fishing ban with Morocco.
newsitem.headline: EU agrees longer fishing ban with Morocco.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday it accepted Morocco's demand to extend an annual selective fishing ban in Moroccan waters to four months, double the current period.
The ban, which protects endangered octopus, squid and cuttlefish stocks, will apply between March and April and between September and October and mainly affects Spanish vessels.
"This measure...will be applied on a non-discriminatory basis to all vessels fishing for cephalopods and associated species in all Morocco's fishing zone," the Commission said in a statement.
A Commission official said that Spanish fishermen would be compensated for the reduction in fishing rights.
The agreement came after four days of talks in Brussels following a suspension of negotiations in December.
Morocco this week seized two Spanish vessels fishing off its coast in an attempt to press the EU to extend the fishing ban.

Last year after months of wrangling, the EU and Morocco hammered out a four-year fisheries agreement under which Brussels agreed to pay Rabat $162.5 million a year in exchange for fishing rights for the mainly Spanish fleet.
